summary: Websocket->SSE fallback intermittently drops final fragment and metadata (customer-visible truncated response)
description:
Issue summary:
Customers on NimbleRetail report repeated cases where a long streaming generation appears to finish, the client falls back from websocket to SSE (due to intermittent network blips) and when the stream reconnects the final token fragment and trailing metadata (e.g., end_of_stream marker and usage/latency footer) are missing. This results in truncated responses or responses where the client never sees the final "done" event.

Impact:
- Multiple customers in the enterprise tier observe end-user replies missing last 1-3 tokens or final JSON metadata.
- Affects production traffic in us-east region.
- Customer reporting visible user-facing truncation in search/assistant experiences.

Environment:
- prod-us-east (cluster: rp-prod-stream-03)
- Customer SDKs: websocket primary, SSE fallback enabled (client library 1.6.2)
- Time window observed: intermittent between 2026-03-08 18:00 UTC and ongoing.

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1. Start a long streaming generation (sequence length ~1k tokens) over websocket to hosted API using the customer SDK with automatic SSE fallback enabled.
2. Simulate a short network interruption (1-3s) or force a websocket close.
3. Client reconnects using SSE and resumes offset resumption if supported.
4. Observe that the resumed stream sometimes ends without the final fragment and without the metadata event.

Observed behavior:
- Final token(s) dropped in ~10-15% of observed reconnections for this customer.
- Missing trailing metadata (usage tokens/latency) in some cases, causing clients to wait for closure event.
- No obvious 5xx at API gateway; logs show upstreams closed connection and streaming-proxy issued a resume attempt.

Expected behavior:
- On fallback/resume the stream should include the entire remainders of the generation plus final metadata/end marker exactly once.

Relevant logs/traces:
- sample request IDs: req-87a3f2, req-87a3f2-resume-1, req-90b2d1
- proxy logs indicate: "client resume request received, resume_offset=512" followed by "upstream stream closed before terminal fragment".
- No obvious runtime OOM; GPU and serving nodes show stable memory.

Temporary workaround provided to customer:
- Recommend customers pinning smaller max_tokens per request or enabling client-side heuristics to accept weakly-terminated responses for now.
- Advised NimbleRetail to toggle SSE-only mode as temporary mitigation if their environment tolerates it.

Next steps / ask from Engineering:
- Capture binary-level tracing of the resume handshake between streaming-proxy and serving-runtime for the listed request IDs.
- Check resume-offset handling codepath for off-by-one on terminal fragment assembly.
- Add additional logging around "terminal fragment emitted" event and metadata footer emission path.

Attachments:
- trimmed proxy log excerpt (attached)
- client side SDK debug dump (attached)
comments: 2026-03-10 09:18 - Janelle Kim: Picked up for triage. Reproduced locally with network emulator; saw a dropped final boundary in one of three attempts. Attaching local traces.

2026-03-10 14:02 - SRE (Ethan Brooks): Verified no node restarts in rp-prod-stream-03. Observed connection resets at load balancer at 18:12 UTC for the same customer IP block; raising with infra networking.
2026-03-11 08:45 - Support (Janelle Kim): Shared recommended workaround with NimbleRetail: enable SSE-only fallback and reduce max_tokens. Customer will test and report.

2026-03-12 11:22 - Eng (Tomas Rivera): Found potential off-by-one in resume offset arithmetic in streaming-proxy v1.4.7. PR drafted to add stricter checks and a gated metric for terminal-fragment-count. See PR #482.
2026-03-12 15:30 - NimbleRetail (Customer): Confirmed reduced frequency of truncation when SSE-only used; still saw one truncated response overnight. Customer requests permanent fix and timeline.
investigation_notes: Checked LB (alb) logs: multiple TLS resets in customer IP range at timestamps that align with observed reconnections.
Tracing: resume handshake includes resume_offset; downstream runtime sometimes returns a close event before terminal fragment packet emitted.
Hypothesis: streaming-proxy may be acknowledging resume and trimming last fragment if upstream closed mid-frame; possible fencepost when assembling last chunk + metadata.
Metric: terminal_fragment_emitted counter shows small drop correlated with websocket-close events for customer-specific traffic pattern.
Action: add debug-only instrumentation to emit sequence id of last emitted fragment and metadata emission boolean to logs in PR branch.
